provenance: Anchors from Hoffmann et al. 2022, 'Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models' (Chinchilla, NeurIPS 2022), which revised Kaplan et al. 2020 (arXiv:2001.08361): for compute-optimal training, model size and training tokens should scale roughly EQUALLY, about 20 tokens per parameter. The two points are the paper's headline comparison at equal training compute -- Gopher, 280B parameters on ~300B tokens (x=280, y=300), versus Chinchilla, 70B parameters on 1.4T tokens (x=70, y=1400) -- where the smaller, data-richer Chinchilla won, averaging 67.5% on MMLU, more than 7 points over Gopher. No curve is digitized or drawn; these are the reported model/token/score anchors only. This is the result that makes TRAINING TOKENS the binding constraint, and so makes the Villalobos et al. data-stock estimate bite.
